Recap (FintechX production flows we covered):
- Primary: customer support assistant (context window ~2k tokens), goal is sub-300ms P95 generation latency for short responses.
- Secondary: document summarization and policy classification (longer sequences, batched).
- Current observed load: ~90 TPS sustained, with daily spikes to ~220 TPS (Tom mentioned a large batch job last week). Attached is the usage snapshot you shared.

Requirements you emphasized:
- Data isolation / VPC requirement for production; on-prem is an option for regulated flows but you'd prefer Dedicated if we can meet isolation + compliance controls.
- SLO targets: P95 latency <300ms for short prompts; acceptable to have higher latency for long summarization jobs.
- Availability: 99.9% SLA for production tier.

Initial sizing notes / unknowns we need:
- Model family you plan to run (we discussed a 13B / 70B family tradeoff).
- Typical token mix: short (<64): ~40%, medium (64-512): ~50%, long (>512): ~10% (please confirm).
- Concurrency per request path and whether you'd prefer separate pools for low-latency vs batch jobs.

Recommended next steps:
1) Can you confirm the token mix and whether the 90 TPS baseline includes only the low-latency path?
2) We'll put together two sizing options (Dedicated GPU pool + Private VPC variant) with rough cost estimates:
   - Option A: Dedicated (hosted Redwood Dedicated) — recommended if you want faster time-to-value + predictable throughput.
   - Option B: Private (VPC / customer-managed) — recommended if you require on-prem/network isolation and Bring-Your-Own-Hardware.
3) Technical follow-up with Dylan (cc'd) to map model choice to GPU type and expected TPS/concurrency.

Attachments: FintechX_usage_snapshot.csv (summary of calls), fintechx_security_qs.pdf (security questionnaire draft).

I'll draft a concrete sizing note after Dylan supplies GPU sizing guidance — aiming to share by Thursday.

Hi Samantha — quick technical notes based on Rafael's recap and your clarifications. TL;DR: two recommended configs depending on model family and whether you want single pool or split pools for latency vs batch.

Assumptions (please flag if different):
- Model family: running a 13B-ish generator for the assistant (LLM-13B equivalent) for low-latency; larger 70B models used only for offline summarization.
- Avg prompt length (assistant): ~120 tokens in, ~40 tokens generated (token mix above).
- Desired concurrency: 8 simultaneous inferences for low-latency pool; batch pool concurrency can be higher with larger sequences.

Sizing guidance (baseline: sustained 120 TPS with headroom to 250 TPS):
Option 1 — Dedicated hosted (recommended for faster setup):
- For 13B generator (quantized, optimized kernels):~
  - 3 x H100 (or equivalently 4 x A100 80GB) in a dedicated pool with autoscale buffer.
  - Per-GPU concurrency tuning: target 6-8 concurrent sessions per GPU for low-latency paths.
  - This gives steady-state headroom to 120 TPS and can absorb spikes to ~250 TPS with autoscale + prewarmed slots.

Option 2 — Private VPC / On-prem (if you provide hardware):
- If you can deploy H100 80GB nodes, start with 3 nodes and plan for an additional 1-2 nodes for peak buffer (4-5 total).
- If constrained to A100 40/80GB, plan for ~4-6 nodes depending on quantization and model footprint.

Performance knobs to reduce required GPU count:
- Quantization (4-bit) + kernel optimizations — often 2-2.5x throughput improvement vs fp16.
- Prefix / KV caching for repeated contexts (support assistant with shared context).
- Separate low-latency pool (smaller sequences) from batch pool (long sequences) — this prevents long jobs from reducing available slots for short calls.

Next steps I can own:
- I'll run a quick benchmark matrix (13B quantized vs 70B quantized) on H100 to give more concrete TPS numbers and expected token/sec.
- Rafael / Marissa: I can produce the two-option sizing doc + ballpark monthly cost delta (hosted Dedicated vs Private VPC) for the deal doc.

Attachments: reference sizing matrix (will share once bench is complete).

— Dylan
